tpl_ai-patrol_begin: Begin Play arms the patrol timer. The route is not stepped from Tick.
tpl_ai-patrol_timer: AdvancePatrol is scheduled about once a second. That is the walk between points.
tpl_ai-patrol_advance: This steps to the next point on the route. Alert from Sense decides whether to leave the route. This function does not decide sight.
tpl_ai-patrol_flip: The route has reached an end, so the direction flag is about to flip.
tpl_ai-patrol_set: GoingRight flips so the next step walks back along the points. A squadmate and a camp use the same idea.
tpl_door_overlap: Someone entered the door volume. That is the start of the swing. Tick does not yaw the door.
tpl_door_timeline: PlayFromStart runs the swing curve. The creak is the audio on that motion, and a horror creak can also poke Sense.
tpl_gas-effect_begin: Begin Play binds the effect dispatcher and arms its timer. Fear or a cost does not broadcast every frame.
tpl_gas-effect_bind: OnEffect now has a listener. When the effect fires, that listener runs. Tick is not the listener.
tpl_gas-effect_timer: The effect is on a one second timer. Cost and cooldown live here, not in a hand-written subtract.
tpl_gas-effect_apply: ApplyEffect runs because the timer elapsed. This is the moment a gameplay effect is allowed to do its work.
tpl_gas-effect_call: OnEffect broadcasts to whoever bound. The character does not also subtract the cost by hand.
tpl_health_dmg: Local, single-player damage. This event is the start of the subtract.
tpl_health_set: Health is clamped between zero and the max. Without the clamp, a big hit goes negative and the death check for exactly zero never sees it.
tpl_health_branch: Death is the zero check after the clamp. It is not a second subtract.
tpl_health_die: The pawn has reached zero health. This is the death signal for this local lesson.
tpl_interact_input: This is the use key. When the player presses interact, this function starts the look. Doors, switches, and pickups only get a chance because this ran. Standing still does not call it.
tpl_interact_trace: This asks the world what the aim hits and stores that hit. The trace is paid once per press, not once per frame.
tpl_interact_branch: This is the hit check. The true pin goes on to Interact. The false pin is a miss and should stop.
tpl_interact_call: This calls Interact on the actor that was hit, through the interface. One call serves a door, a switch, or a pickup.
tpl_interact_miss: This is the miss. It logs that there was nothing to use and does not open, damage, or save anything.
tpl_inventory-slot_overlap: Overlap is the pickup. Walking into the item is what asks the slot to take it. The use trace does not count.
tpl_inventory-slot_branch: The stack only transfers when the count is already positive. An empty overlap does not invent an item.
tpl_inventory-slot_call: AddToSlot goes through the interface. The slot owns the count. The pickup only asks.
tpl_inventory-slot_store: After a successful add, the local count is cleared so the same overlap cannot add twice.
tpl_pickup-wait_input: The use key started a delayed pickup. The grant waits out the delay.
tpl_pickup-wait_delay: The delay is a timer, not a Tick. When it finishes, the cast and the interface call run.
tpl_pickup-wait_cast: The cast checks the actor is the kind of thing that can receive the pickup call.
tpl_pickup-wait_call: The interface call actually grants the item after the delay.
tpl_pickup_overlap: Walking into the pickup is the event. It is not a use-key press.
tpl_pickup_set: Ammo goes up by one. That is the whole gift of this pickup.
tpl_pickup_destroy: The pickup actor is removed so the same can cannot be collected twice.
tpl_replicated-health_damage: This is the damage event. It is the only honest place to start a health change. Tick must not subtract health.
tpl_replicated-health_auth: A component asks its owner who has authority. Only that machine may write Health. Clients can ask. They do not subtract.
tpl_replicated-health_set: This stores the new health on the authority. Everyone else will hear it through replication, not by running this line.
tpl_replicated-health_rep: OnRep runs on the other machines when Health arrives. It is the moment to play the hit. It must not subtract again.
tpl_replicated-health_show: This is the local feedback after replication. The float was already decided.
tpl_save-load_begin: Begin Play is the load, not the save. It reads a struct that some earlier event already wrote.
tpl_save-load_make: This builds the little struct that stands in for the saved values. Tick should not be filling it every frame.
tpl_save-load_store: The struct's stand-in value is stored on the slot. A real save writes this when an event finishes, then Begin Play reads it back.
tpl_save-load_load: This is the load function Begin Play calls. It unpacks the slot. It does not replay the actions that earned those numbers.
tpl_save-load_break: Breaking the struct pulls the saved fields back out so the component can apply them once.
tpl_save-load_show: The load finished. This log is the local confirmation, not another write.
tpl_tactical-ammo_input: This is reload. It runs when the player asks to reload, then checks the magazine and the reserve before any round moves.
tpl_tactical-ammo_branch: Both checks live here: the magazine is not full, and the reserve is not empty. Fail either one and the reload stops.
tpl_tactical-ammo_setneed: Needed is how many rounds will fit. It is clamped so you cannot load more than the empty space and cannot load more than you carry.
tpl_tactical-ammo_setmag: This is Set Magazine. It adds Needed into the magazine. It has to come after the clamp, or the mag would overfill.
tpl_tactical-ammo_setres: This takes the same Needed out of reserve. The rounds moved. They were not copied.
tpl_tactical-ammo_nope: The reload was refused. The mag was full or the reserve was empty, so no number changes.
tpl_timer_begin: Begin Play arms a timer. The work is not a Tick override.
tpl_timer_arm: The timer is scheduled. When it fires, the named function runs once.
tpl_timer_tick: This is the timer callback, not an engine Tick. The name is historical. It runs because the timer elapsed.
tpl_timer_print: The callback's visible trace. It prints because the timer fired.
tpl_timer_again: The callback arms the timer again. That is a loop on a clock, still not a frame Tick.
tpl_aoi_begin: Begin Play arms the interest timer. Relevance is not the fog bit and it is not Tick.
tpl_aoi_timer: CheckAOI runs about twice a second. Distant pawns drop out on this clock.
tpl_aoi_check: One interest pass. The trace result becomes Relevant.
tpl_aoi_auth: Relevant is a server decision. Clients do not mark themselves in range.
tpl_aoi_trace: The interest trace. A hit means this actor still matters to the match.
tpl_aoi_set: Relevant stores the trace result. Copying Visible into Relevant would mix fog with replication range.
tpl_artillery_event: FireMission is the gun order. It traces an impact and spends a shell. It does not lift fog.
tpl_artillery_auth: Shells are shared ammo. Only the authority spends one.
tpl_artillery_trace: The impact trace for this mission. The shell is spent because a mission was fired, not because Tick ran.
tpl_artillery_set: Shells drops by one. Supplies is the economy float and must not be used as a shell.
tpl_ballistics_input: This is the fire button. One press, one trace. Aiming is a different action and does not add heat.
tpl_ballistics_trace: The shot. It asks what the barrel is pointing at, once.
tpl_ballistics_branch: Heat is added only when the shot hits. A miss does not warm the barrel in this excerpt.
tpl_ballistics_set: Heat rises by 0.05 on a hit. Wear can key off this number later. Tick must not add 0.05 while the player is only aiming.
tpl_camera_input: This is aim, from the shoulder camera. It does not fire and it does not interact.
tpl_camera_trace: The aim trace starts at the camera, because a chest trace would hit the cover the crosshair can see past.
tpl_camera_branch: A camera hit is what allows Aiming to become true. A miss leaves the shoulder where it was.
tpl_camera_set: Aiming is now true. Motion matching may read it. The weapon graph is not this write.
tpl_economy_event: Spend is an event, not a tick. A building, a unit, or a bill asks to pay a data cost.
tpl_economy_auth: Supplies are shared. Only the authority subtracts them. Each client subtracting would drain the stock once per machine.
tpl_economy_set: Supplies drops by the data cost, 25 in this excerpt. Shells are a different budget and must not use this float.
tpl_fog_begin: Begin Play arms Reveal. Fog is a team fact updated a few times a second, not every frame.
tpl_fog_timer: Reveal is scheduled at about a quarter of a second. That is the vision pass.
tpl_fog_reveal: One vision pass. A trace decides whether this unit is seen.
tpl_fog_trace: The vision trace. A hit means the team can see the target.
tpl_fog_branch: The hit bool gates the write. A miss does not mark the target visible.
tpl_fog_set: Visible becomes true for the team. A client must not write this to cheat the fog.
tpl_gunsmith_input: This is equip. The player picked a slot. The id is what other machines need, not the meshes.
tpl_gunsmith_auth: EquippedId is shared state. Only the authority writes it, or proxies pop the wrong gun.
tpl_gunsmith_set: EquippedId becomes the slot the player chose. Ten visual slots can live in a data asset. This one id replicates.
tpl_movement_input: This is the move key or stick. Speed changes only because the axis changed, which is what the animation later reads as the gait.
tpl_movement_branch: This asks whether the stick is pushed. Pushed means sprint speed. Released means walk speed.
tpl_movement_sprint: This stores a sprint speed of 600. Motion matching and the third-person gait read this number. They do not trace.
tpl_movement_walk: This stores a walk speed of 200 when the stick is released. The camera does not write this.
tpl_orders_input: This is the order button. It does not search the whole level. It looks at the unit in hand.
tpl_orders_branch: Selected is the gate. An unselected unit does not receive the order, even if the cursor is on it.
tpl_orders_call: ReceiveOrder runs on the selected unit. Formation offsets stay data. They are not written here.
tpl_perception_begin: Begin Play arms the Sense timer. The hunter does not trace on the first frame and then every frame.
tpl_perception_timer: Sense is scheduled at a fraction of a second. A wall, a glimpse, and a loud sound all share this timer instead of a second brain.
tpl_perception_sense: This is one Sense pass: a trace. Alert becomes 1 only if that trace is clear.
tpl_perception_trace: The hunter's look. It starts at the hunter and stops at a wall. The player's interact trace is a different function.
tpl_perception_branch: A clear line of sight takes the true pin. A blocked trace leaves Alert alone.
tpl_perception_set: Alert is set to 1 because the trace hit. A creak can call this same event. It should not grow a second AI.
tpl_scoring_event: AwardMedal is the event that earns points. The scoreboard widget only listens.
tpl_scoring_auth: Score is shared. The authority adds the medal value. A client adding 10 would desync the board.
tpl_scoring_set: Score increases by the data value, 10 in this excerpt. OnRep must refresh the widget and must not add 10 again.
tpl_vehicle-drive_input: This is the throttle axis. It is not the on-foot move axis. A sprint must not pedal the truck.
tpl_vehicle-drive_auth: Throttle is shared on a driven vehicle. The authority writes it.
tpl_vehicle-drive_set: Throttle becomes the axis value. Speed, the on-foot gait number, stays a different variable.
